title: Amazon Leo adds 6 new Arianespace launches, expanding its launch partnership
summary: The agreement extends the largest commercial contract in Arianespace history and supports investment and innovation across Europe.
body_markdown:
---


## Key takeaways


- Amazon Leo is adding six new Ariane 6 launches, expanding its total Arianespace commitment from 18 to 24 launches.


- Arianespace has delivered 100 Amazon Leo satellites to orbit across three missions in less than five months.


- Long-term launch agreements support hundreds of suppliers and thousands of highly skilled jobs across Europe.


---


[Amazon Leo](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/amazon-leo) is expanding its launch commitment with Arianespace, adding six new Ariane 6 contracts and bringing total contracted launch capacity from 18 to 24 launches.


[Inside Amazon Leo's Florida hub: Preparing satellites for Amazon's space network](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/innovation-at-amazon/project-kuiper-florida-satellite-facility)


Amazon’s $140 million site at Kennedy Space Center can support up to three simultaneous launch campaigns for its satellite internet network.


Amazon Leo is a key customer for Arianespace, the world’s first commercial launch service provider, and the new agreement extends what was already the largest commercial contract in the company's history. The expanded commitment provides a long-term demand signal that supports the continued ramp-up of Ariane 6 and helps Arianespace grow launch capacity for commercial and institutional customers.


## Expanding Amazon Leo’s partnership with Arianespace


Encapsulated Amazon Leo satellites arrive at the launch pad for integration with Ariane 6 ahead of liftoff.


Photo by Arianespace


Amazon


[first signed with Arianespace](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/innovation-at-amazon/amazon-makes-historic-launch-investment-to-advance-project-kuiper) in 2022, part of a record-breaking set of agreements to secure more than 80 launches. Arianespace flew its first mission for Amazon earlier this year, and has now delivered 100 Leo satellites to orbit across three missions.


The most recent mission,


[Leo Europe 3 (LE-03)](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/amazon-leo/amazon-leo-rocket-satellite-update) , deployed 36 satellites using upgraded P160C solid boosters developed by ArianeGroup, making it the largest Amazon Leo mission to date and the heaviest commercial payload ever launched on any rocket.


These new boosters increase Ariane 6's payload capacity by up to two metric tons, and Amazon Leo and Arianespace engineering teams are working side by side to further increase the number of satellites deployed per launch through vehicle upgrades as the constellation scales.


[Amazon to acquire Globalstar and expand Amazon Leo satellite network](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/company-news/amazon-globalstar-apple)


Globalstar satellites, radio frequency spectrum, and operational expertise will enable Amazon Leo to add Direct-to-Device (D2D) services to future generations of its low Earth orbit satellite network.


"Europe isn't just a region we are going to serve. Europe's launch infrastructure is part of the operational architecture of the Amazon Leo constellation," said Chris Weber, vice president of Amazon Leo business and product. "We committed early because we believed in what Arianespace was building, and they've executed mission after mission. Expanding from 18 to 24 launches reflects our confidence in Ariane 6 and our continued investment in European launch capability."


Ariane 6 is assembled and launched from French Guiana, but its supply chain runs across 13 European countries and more than 600 companies. Amazon Leo is Arianespace's largest single customer, and Oxford Economics estimates the associated EU spending will contribute €2.8 billion to GDP and support an average of 3,270 jobs annually through 2029.


“We are delighted to reach this new stage in our partnership with Amazon Leo. These six additional launches demonstrate Amazon Leo’s confidence in the performance and reliability of Ariane 6, as well as in the expertise of our teams,” said David Cavaillolès, CEO of Arianespace.


Amazon Leo satellites arrive at Europe's Spaceport in French Guiana for processing and launch after traveling from Amazon Leo's satellite processing facility in Cape Canaveral, Florida.


Photo by Arianespace


“Long-term commitments from customers such as Amazon Leo support the ramp-up of Ariane 6 and strengthen our business model. They increase our capacity to serve all our customers while ensuring Europe has the capabilities it needs to deploy its critical space infrastructure. Ariane 6’s strength lies in its ability to serve both commercial and institutional missions.”


[Amazon Leo is the third-largest satellite constellation in operation](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/innovation-at-amazon/what-is-amazon-project-kuiper) . The company has completed 14 missions since full-scale deployment began in April 2025, putting


[nearly 400 satellites into orbit](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/innovation-at-amazon/project-kuiper-satellite-rocket-launch-progress-updates) . The network is designed to deliver fast, reliable internet to customers and communities beyond the reach of existing networks.


Amazon Leo deploys its constellation across multiple launch vehicles, with more than 100 launches secured. The company is preparing for an initial service rollout this year, with plans to expand globally as coverage and capacity increase.
